elements.label: Figure 4.3
elements.description: Chart type: scatter plot with a fitted linear trend line, one point per country. X-axis: "Log Real GDP Per Capita at PPP", ticks 6 to 12 (in steps of 1). Y-axis: "Fraction under 5 not stunted", ticks 50% to 100% (in steps of 10%). Points are teal for most countries, orange for labeled comparators, and a blue point marks Vietnam. Labeled points: Thailand (~9.8, ~90%), Malaysia (~10.2, ~80%), Indonesia (~9.4, ~73%), Vietnam (~9.0, ~76%), Philippines (~8.0, ~80%), Cambodia (~7.5, ~68%), Lao PDR (~9.0, ~71%), Myanmar (~8.7, ~70%). Values are approximate readings written with "~"; no values are printed on the chart. Pattern: the share of children not stunted rises with GDP per capita, with a positive trend line running from about 65% at log GDP 6 to about 84% at log GDP 12. Vietnam sits near the trend line, while several low-income countries fall to 50–65%.

elements.label: Figure 4.4
elements.description: Chart type: scatter plot with a fitted linear trend line, one point per country. X-axis: "Log Real GDP Per Capita at PPP", ticks 6 to 12 (in steps of 1). Y-axis: "Survival Rate Age 15–60", ticks 50% to 100% (in steps of 10%). Points are teal for most countries, orange for labeled comparators, and a blue point marks Vietnam. Labeled points: Singapore (~11.5, ~95%), Thailand (~9.8, ~88%), Malaysia (~10.2, ~86%), Indonesia (~9.7, ~84%), Vietnam (~9.0, ~86%), Philippines (~8.0, ~83%), Cambodia (~8.3, ~84%), Lao PDR (~9.2, ~80%), Myanmar (~8.7, ~80%). Values are approximate readings written with "~"; no values are printed on the chart. Pattern: survival rates increase with GDP per capita, with a positive trend line from about 78% at log GDP 6 to about 88% at log GDP 11.5; most countries cluster between 75% and 95%, with a few low outliers near 50–65%.
